newsitem.title: FRANCE: STET sale seen before end Oct - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: STET sale seen before end Oct - Le Monde.

text.p: The privatisation of Italian telecoms group STET is seen taking place before the end of October despite a parliamentary defeat of government sale plans last week, chairman Ernesto Pascale told Le Monde.

"I think it will happen before the end of October. The precise date has not been fixed. The privatisation is the best thing to do and it has to be as quick as possible because we are in an uncomfortable position," Pascale said in an interview.
"We are no longer considered as belonging to the state but we are not private either," he added.

Last week the neo-communists, part of the governing majority but against privatisations, abstained from voting and delivered a parliamentary defeat to a plan to transfer the STET sales to the Italian Treasury from the IRI holding group.

Pascale said he did not believe the setback would handicap the STET sale, noting the transfer could also be done via a decree but he added a political solution needed to be found to keep the neo-communists on board.
Pascale said that terms of the planned merger between STET and Telecom Italia should be known between the end of June and the end of August.
He did not exclude the merger would take the form of STET acquiring Telecom Italia because STET already has a listing in New York.

Pascale said that at the privatisation of the merged group there would be a core group of shareholders which would be "formed by private Italian shareholders and a significant presence of foreign investors".
He did not exclude the entry of a foreign operator in the share capital but noted that an industrial accord needed to be a condition for such an entry.
Pascale also said that he would resign after the privatisation. "With a change of owner, the task of a manager is to offer his resignation," he told the newspaper.
